question: What is the main goal of musculoskeletal diagnostic tests?

options.A: Identify bone and soft tissue disorders

explanation: Diagnostic tests help find structural damage, inflammation, or disease in the bones, joints, and muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is a physical examination done before ordering advanced imaging tests?

options.A: It eliminates the need for laboratory work
options.B: It is required by hospital insurance policy
options.C: It prevents all potential post-procedure pain
options.D: It guides the selection of the correct test

explanation: Clinical findings help nurses and doctors decide whether a patient needs an X-ray, an MRI, or blood work. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h1)

question: Standard X-rays are most effective for visualizing which bodily structure?
explanation: Dense structures like bone absorb radiation well, making X-rays ideal for skeletal fractures and joint margins. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which diagnostic test is usually ordered to check a patient for osteoporosis?
explanation: A DEXA scan measures bone mineral density to help diagnose osteoporosis and track treatment progress. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h2)

question: An MRI is best used to look at which type of body tissue?

options.A: Soft tissues like ligaments and cartilage

explanation: MRI creates clear pictures of water-rich soft tissues, making it the top choice for checking injured ligaments and cartilage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does a hot spot on a nuclear medicine bone scan indicate?

options.A: Areas of increased bone turnover or activity
options.B: Complete absence of blood supply to tissue

explanation: Tracers accumulate heavily in regions of high metabolic activity, such as healing fractures, infection, or tumors. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main tool used during an arthroscopic examination of a joint?

options.A: A fiber-optic scope inserted into the joint
options.C: Surface electrodes placed over muscle bellies
options.D: A large-bore needle for joint aspiration

explanation: Arthroscopy uses a tiny, lighted scope so the surgeon can directly look inside the joint space. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do doctors often choose arthroscopy instead of traditional open joint surgery?

options.A: It eliminates the need for post-procedure care
options.B: It involves smaller incisions and faster recovery
options.C: It can only be performed on outpatient adults
options.D: It requires no form of anesthesia whatsoever

explanation: Making smaller cuts causes less trauma to the body, leading to less pain and a quicker return to normal activities. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is inserted into the muscle during an electromyography (EMG) test?
explanation: EMG uses fine needle electrodes to measure the electrical activity and health of skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h5)

question: A patient has numbness and tingling in the hand from a suspected pinched nerve. Which test is best?
explanation: Nerve conduction studies check how fast electrical signals travel through a nerve, helping find problems like carpal tunnel syndrome. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the medical term for withdrawing fluid from a joint space?
explanation: Arthrocentesis involves placing a needle into the joint cavity to draw out synovial fluid for testing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which finding in joint fluid confirms a diagnosis of gout?
explanation: Finding uric acid crystals under a microscope in the synovial fluid confirms gouty arthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which allergy must a nurse check for before a patient receives intravenous contrast dye?
explanation: Many contrast dyes contain iodine, so patients with a history of shellfish or iodine allergies are at risk for a reaction. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is a vital safety check before a patient enters the MRI room?

options.A: Starting an intravenous line with heavy fluids
options.B: Removing all metallic objects from the patient
options.C: Administering a local anesthetic to the skin
options.D: Testing the patient for active joint infections

explanation: The strong magnet in an MRI machine can pull metal objects toward it with dangerous force, making metal removal essential. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which assessment is most important after a patient has an invasive procedure on an arm or leg?
explanation: Checking pulses, skin color, temperature, and feeling in the limb ensures that blood flow and nerve function are normal after the procedure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is a key sign that a patient is developing an infection after joint surgery or aspiration?

options.B: Mild bruising around the needle site

explanation: Pain, warmth, redness, and swelling that get worse over days rather than better can point to an infection in the joint or wound. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h8)
